english.title: Fail to make a written report following the report of a serious adverse event at a clinical trial

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: Medicines for Human Use Clinical Trials Regulations 2004

english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) being the investigator in relation to a clinical trial, failed to make a detailed written report on a serious adverse event following the immediate report of that event, which occurred in a subject, namely **(..SPECIFY THE NAME OF THE SUBJECT..) at a trial site at which you were responsible
english.legislation: Contrary to regulation 32(3), 49(1)(g) and 52 of the Medicines for Human Use (Clinical Trials) Regulations 2004.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
contravened a provision of regulation 32 of the Medicines for Human Use(Clinical Trials) Regulations 2004
by the investigator failing to make
a detailed written report
following the immediate report of a serious adverse event

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Regulation 51 of the of the Medicines for Human Use (Clinical Trials) Regulations 2004 provides a defence of due diligence.
(ii) This offence no longer applies from the 27th April 2026 due to changes made by the Medicines for Human Use (Clinical Trials) (Amendment) Regulations 2025. For the offence applicable after this date, see H102703..

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 3 months imprisonment and / or a fine
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment and / or a fine

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
